pr_title: Fix GDScript autocompletion with "as" or typed variables

issue_context.title: Explicit types break contextual autocompletion
issue_context.body:

**Godot version:**
4f6eb36

**Issue description:**
...at least for AnimationPlayer. Here's a typed AnimationPlayer node variable:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/64057712-b564d180-cba0-11e9-8bb5-b8bf8ea27093.png)
Works as expected. But when we enforce the type to make sure it's AnimationPlayer:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/64057713-c01f6680-cba0-11e9-8b2d-86c926ac2b8a.png)
The animations don't show.
comments: Does it work with `onready var anim : AnimationPlayer = $AnimationPlayer`?
Huh, it actually works. So only using `as` causes problems in this case.

This is actually closely related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/33434#issuecomment-559147462. When you use `as`, the variable loses the original context, even if it's converted to the same type.
@bojidar-bg Um, looks like #34286 didn't fix this.
@KoBeWi Oh yeah? Mind if you give a reproduction example or project? :)
Weird, it actually works in a minimal project. I'll look into it if it happens again.

This has cherrypick 3.2 label, so it would be nice if someone could find which commit fixed the issue, but otherwise it can be closed.
Seems fixed in the 3.2 branch too (b929f561d), the fix was likely cherry-picked.

review_comments: Do we really need to check the source node? We already have a resulting type from the cast as `cn->cast_type`, we should be able to just use that. Unless we use the actual type of `source_node` in this case.
We need the value from the source node, so that `($x as AnimationPlayer).play(..` autocompletes with animation names from `$x`.
